items.title: Lionel Ferbos Interview, 1964-08-03
items.q: And that's where I put Andrew Morgan in my place at the Happy Land.

ctx.x: Well first I worked with Idru Coleman, and Albert Giles, and what's that called bass band? Dorsley. Eddie Dorsley. And then after a while, that's when I told you, I left and went back with you again. That's right. And when I went back with him again, after I went with him a while, I know something happened, I think the job ran out over there.

When you came back to the Melody Inn when I had the band in charge, this man would close up and went back to the Happy Land. Yeah, that's right. And then when he came back to the Happy Land, the Melody Inn opened again, I went back to the Melody Inn. And that's where I put Andrew Morgan in my place at the Happy Land.
That's right. And I worked with Andrew Morgan. Was the same outfit with the exception of Idru Coleman?

items.title: Andrew Morgan Interview, 1961-07-04
items.q: Harold Dejan's always talking about him, he's wonderful.

ctx.x: Well, he was only charging, uh, a half a dollar for lessons. How often did you go? Once a week or twice? Well, then we could go, no, we was, we were taking lessons twice a week with him. Twice a week. Twice a week with him. That was the price, Ron, you know, on lessons at that time. 50 cents. 50 cents. So, Joe Watson, he gave me a lesson on the clarinet, well he didn't charge me anything. Pinchback Churro, well I paid him a half a dollar. David Jones, it was a half a dollar. And, Ennis Band, and Earl Fosch here…
Harold Dejan's always talking about him, he's wonderful. Yeah.

He's a wonderful saxophone player. Well then he gave me a lot of ideas about playing the tenor saxophone, because he showed my old fingering on the saxophone, and him and I used to sit down and play duets together. Well then, I played with some of that. For sure.
